data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's causal mechanism is underspecified and its within-evaluation discriminator is invalid. The claim asserts that aggregation cancels idiosyncratic noise while preserving 'the checklist's systematic signal,' but it never establishes what causal mechanism makes the checklist's signal veridical rather than merely systematic bias. The proposed single-evaluation test — members reaching the same answer via different checklist-item subsets indicates 'genuine understanding' — has no causal warrant: convergent answers from heterogeneous item subsets can arise from correlated non-causal cues (e.g., all items keyed to a surface feature), and the target offers no mechanism connecting item-subset diversity to tracking the true outcome-generating process.
